recall_prompt: Say how you would answer this — give the definition in set form, and say what example you would show it on.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: State the definition
steps.margin_note: First mark. The line that earns it is A Δ B = (A − B) ∪ (B − A). Both differences must appear, and they must be joined by a union.
lines: Let A and B be two sets.
The symmetric difference of A and B, written A Δ B, is
So A Δ B is the set of elements that lie in exactly one of A and B.

recall.must_convey: That A Δ B = (A − B) ∪ (B − A), the elements lying in exactly one of the two sets.
accept: A delta B is A minus B union B minus A
the elements that are in one set but not in both
state it as the union of the two differences
symmetric difference ante A minus B union B minus A
take both differences and join them with a union

steps.why: A definition question is marked on the exact statement, so both differences and the union between them have to be on the page. Getting the definition right also fixes the example that follows.
steps.memory_tip: Symmetric difference means in one set or the other, but not in both.
common_mistakes: Writing only A − B and calling that the symmetric difference.
Writing A ∪ B, which keeps the shared elements as well.
Using an intersection in place of the union of the two differences.

steps.label: Show it on an example
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Two small sets are enough. The examiner looks for the shared element being dropped, so choose sets that actually share one.
lines: 3 lies in both sets, so it is not included.

recall.must_convey: That an example is worked and the shared element is left out, giving A Δ B = {1, 2, 4}.
accept: take A as one two three and B as three four so the answer is one two four
three is in both sets so it is dropped
work a small example and remove the common element
common element ni theesi migilina vaatini rayali
the answer is one two four

steps.why: The example shows the definition has been understood and not only memorised. The element 3 being dropped is the part that separates the symmetric difference from the union.
steps.memory_tip: Remove whatever the two sets share, then keep everything else.
common_mistakes: Keeping 3 in the answer, which gives A ∪ B instead.
Computing only B − A and writing {4} as the answer.
Choosing two sets with no common element, so the example proves nothing.
